grh_8cbaf87870d711dea610.title: Best Foot Forward
paragraphs: Prep-school student Bud Hooper jokingly invites movie star Gale Joy to his prom and panics when she unexpectedly accepts, especially because he has lied to his regular girlfriend Helen that he is ill. Gale attends under Helen's name in search of publicity, while the real Helen arrives and the deception erupts into scandal. The principal expels Bud, but Gale protects him by threatening a publicity photograph that would embarrass the school. When the prom story becomes national news, the principal reverses the punishment, and Bud and Helen reconcile with plans to marry.

The cast includes Gordon MacRae, Jerome Cowan, Betty Garrett, Joseph Kearns, and Alice Pearce. Other credited names include Jerome Lawrence as radio adaptor, Robert E. Lee as radio adaptor, Gordon MacRae as host, and Marvin Miller as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 45 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.f7185f50dd01455d|Association of American Railroads]].
This version dramatizes [[work|work.rr.5dee83cc59186913|Best Foot Forward]]. Jerome Lawrence adapted it for radio and Robert E. Lee adapted it for radio.

grh_8c4a45aa4d2687aff2d8.title: The Rudolph Friml Story
paragraphs: This dramatized biography follows Rudolf Friml from a baker's family in Prague, where an unexpected piano awakens his talent, through conservatory training and his early ambitions as a composer. A youthful romance and the guidance of established musicians shape the melodies he later carries to America, where he is first known as a concert pianist and serious composer. A theatrical dispute unexpectedly gives him the chance to write for the stage, leading to successful operettas including The Firefly and later works remembered throughout the program. The tribute ends with Friml himself joining the broadcast and playing music from his newest Broadway work.

grh_8c252e8c143682430111.title: Going Down
paragraphs: Ernie takes his wife Emma deep beneath the city into service tunnels and sub-basements, secretly intending to kill her and then himself. Their plan is overtaken by something far stranger when a blind creature from beneath the earth begins stalking them through the dark. grh_8cb8eccc86afa5874512.title: Double Indemnity
paragraphs: Rocky answers a chauffeur ad, is knocked unconscious and wakes in a wealthy household where everyone insists he is Steve Crandell, husband of Laura and holder of a large life-insurance policy. He learns that the household is trying to use him as a substitute corpse in a double-indemnity scheme devised by the real Steve, Laura and their accomplices. grh_8cc4e823a0db7d0d2f67.title: The Necklace
paragraphs: Mathilde longs for the elegance she cannot afford and borrows a glittering necklace for a grand evening. When the necklace disappears, she and her husband secretly replace it with an expensive duplicate and spend fourteen years sacrificing their youth and comfort to repay the debt. grh_8c50070a1a034cb64161.title: Headquarters Budapest
paragraphs: A dramatization based on Robert Parker's Headquarters Budapest uses satire and reported scenes to examine corruption, dictatorship and political weakness in the prewar Balkans. The program portrays rulers such as Prince Paul, King Carol and other regional leaders as divided from their own people while Hitler exploits economic dependence, territorial rivalries and authoritarian politics to extend German influence. Parker closes by warning that another world war could again begin in the Balkans unless the region receives education, economic opportunity, democratic government and a coherent postwar policy from the major Allied powers.

grh_8cee8d3d8df85403e4d9.title: Mr Kramer-Parker Needs a Hobby
paragraphs: Nurse Parker takes up painting as a hobby after one of her battles with Gillespie and becomes acutely ill after spending meals and spare time surrounded by oil paints, even dipping her brush into her coffee; Kildare recognizes mild lead poisoning. Her case supplies the clue to Mr. Kramer's puzzling new symptoms on top of chronic arthritis: his recently installed furnace recovers precious metal from jewelry sweepings by using litharge, or lead oxide, and has been slowly poisoning him as well; both patients begin treatment while Parker's much-ridiculed painting unexpectedly wins an art prize.

This [[show|dr-kildare|Dr. Kildare]] broadcast aired on November 24, 1950. The cast includes Lew Ayres, Lionel Barrymore, [[person|virginia-gregg|Virginia Gregg]], [[person|georgia-ellis|Georgia Ellis]], and Ben Wright. Other credited names include William P. Rousseau as director, Raymond Katz as producer, Les Crutchfield as writer, and Dick Joy as announcer.
